cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: You Handle the Evidence
cards.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Keep the raffle cashbox in your office till the treasurer comes. I can't face explaining the broken lock.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then take it home. You can hand it to her tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll want me to count it with her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You handle the count and explain the lock; I'll send you the key that snapped.

mechanism: A uses assumed supervisory authority to transfer both custody of evidence and the uncomfortable explanation to B.
confusable: Unlike useful delegation with shared responsibility, A explicitly cannot face the explanation and progressively assigns it away.
comparison: Cashbox custody, count and snapped key differ from chasing a missing service receipt.
seedUse: The seed already commands storage, removal and explanation; S01 supports the actual transfer rather than only adding a mood.
